# KS-865 — Wednesday's task for Ornith, BASH_PATCH (the first script ticket; written 00:39 on 2026-09-16 from the file at develop M55 `48e65c435` — `scripts/check-no-latest-tags.sh` lines 1–59 read WHOLE; `scripts/__tests__/check_script_portability.test.sh` lines 1–40 read for the suite shape; `git ls-tree` at the tip: `.github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml` exists NEITHER at the repo root NOR under `Blockchain/Dev`)

## What is wrong (one paragraph)
`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-no-latest-tags.sh` advertises six files (`CHECK_FILES`, :32–39) and at :42 `[ -f "$f" ] || continue`
skips a missing one SILENTLY, then prints `OK` (:56) — so it scans five of six and cannot fail on the sixth. The sixth,
`.github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml` (:38), does not exist anywhere at the tip (the workflow is retired). The ticket's
acceptance: a listed input that is missing is an ERROR, not a skip, and the script REPORTS how many of the advertised files it
examined. **This task: four small edits to the script — count what is scanned, refuse a missing listed input, drop the dead
entry (with a one-line comment naming why), and print the count on the OK line — plus one new shell suite that proves it.**
NOT in this task: `run-code-guards.sh` (the caller), any other script, the `:latest` grep itself (:45–47 stay).

## The exact change — FOUR SMALL EDITS in `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-no-latest-tags.sh` (they fall into two hunks: :27–:45 and :53–:59)
E1 — INSERT one line after line 30 `EXIT=0` (context: line 29 is blank, line 31 is blank, line 32 is `CHECK_FILES=(`):
```
 EXIT=0
+SCANNED=0
 
```
E2 — line 38 `  ".github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml"` is REPLACED by one comment line (context: line 37 is `  "deployment/azure/main.parameters.json"`, line 39 is `)`):
```
   "deployment/azure/main.parameters.json"
-  ".github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml"
+  # KS-865: .github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml was listed here but exists nowhere at the tip (the workflow is retired); a missing listed input is now an ERROR below, so a dead entry cannot ride along.
 )
```
E3 — line 42 `  [ -f "$f" ] || continue` is REPLACED by six lines (context: line 41 is `for f in "${CHECK_FILES[@]}"; do`, line 43 is `  # Match \`image: …:latest\` or \`imageTag: latest\` or \`:latest"\` in JSON.`):
```
 for f in "${CHECK_FILES[@]}"; do
-  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
+  if [ ! -f "$f" ]; then
+    echo "::error::$f is listed in CHECK_FILES but does not exist under $ROOT (KS-865: a missing input is an error, not a skip)"
+    EXIT=1
+    continue
+  fi
+  SCANNED=$((SCANNED+1))
   # Match `image: …:latest` or `imageTag: latest` or `:latest"` in JSON.
```
E4 — line 56 is REPLACED (context: line 55 is `if [ $EXIT -eq 0 ]; then`, line 57 is `fi`):
```
 if [ $EXIT -eq 0 ]; then
-  echo "OK — no :latest tags found in production-bound configs."
+  echo "OK — no :latest tags found in production-bound configs ($SCANNED of ${#CHECK_FILES[@]} advertised files examined)."
 fi
```
Every `+` line above is byte-exact — copy it; do not paraphrase the comment, do not re-indent (two spaces inside the loop, four inside the if), do not add a trailing comment. Nothing else in the script changes.

## The test — ONE NEW shell suite, bash 3.2, beside the reference
File: `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/check_no_latest_tags_inputs.test.sh`
Copy the SHAPE of `scripts/__tests__/check_script_portability.test.sh`: `#!/usr/bin/env bash`, a header comment naming KS-865, `set -uo pipefail`, `PASS=0; FAIL=0`, `TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT`, and its closing lines that print the totals and `exit 1` when FAIL is not 0. The script under test is located as `GATE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)/check-no-latest-tags.sh"`. The script resolves its root from ITS OWN location (`ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"` then `cd "$ROOT"`), so every case COPIES it into a throwaway tree and creates the listed files there. Write this helper VERBATIM (text to copy):
```
# make_case <name> <files to create, space-separated, relative to the case root> — copies the gate into <case>/scripts/
# and creates each listed file (empty). Prints the case root.
make_case() {
  local name="$1"; shift; local d="$TMP/$name"
  mkdir -p "$d/scripts" && cp "$GATE" "$d/scripts/check-no-latest-tags.sh" && chmod +x "$d/scripts/check-no-latest-tags.sh"
  local f; for f in "$@"; do mkdir -p "$d/$(dirname "$f")" && : > "$d/$f"; done
  echo "$d"
}
# run_case <case root> — runs the copied gate; sets OUT and RC.
run_case() { OUT=$(bash "$1/scripts/check-no-latest-tags.sh" 2>&1); RC=$?; }
# check <name> <want_rc> <want_substring> — one cell: exit code AND a substring of the output.
check() {
  local name="$1" want="$2" sub="$3"
  if [ "$RC" -ne "$want" ]; then FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); echo "  FAIL: $name (expected exit $want, got $RC)"; return; fi
  case "$OUT" in *"$sub"*) PASS=$((PASS+1)); echo "  PASS: $name" ;; *) FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); echo "  FAIL: $name (exit ok, output lacks '$sub')" ;; esac
}
ALL="docker-compose.production.yml deployment/azure/services.bicep deployment/azure/services.parameters.json deployment/azure/main.bicep deployment/azure/main.parameters.json"
```
Cells (every cell 🔴 or CONTROL, nothing optional), each built with `make_case`, run with `run_case`, asserted with `check`:
- 🔴 `check "🔴 KS-865 — a listed input that is missing is an error" 1 "does not exist"`: the case creates ALL of `$ALL` except `deployment/azure/main.bicep` (four files). (Untouched script: the missing file is skipped and the gate exits 0 with OK — the red.)
- 🔴 `check "🔴 KS-865 — the OK line reports how many advertised files were examined" 0 "5 of 5 advertised files examined"`: the case creates all five of `$ALL`, all empty. (Untouched script: exit 0 but the OK line carries no count — the red.)
- CONTROL `check "KS-865 control — a :latest tag in a listed file is still refused" 1 "::error::"`: all five created, then `printf 'image: foo:latest\n' > "$d/docker-compose.production.yml"` before running. Green on both trees.
- CONTROL `check "KS-865 control — a comment-only :latest is ignored" 0 "OK"`: all five created, then `printf '# image: foo:latest\n' > "$d/docker-compose.production.yml"`. Green on both trees.
Use `d=$(make_case case1 $ALL_MINUS_ONE)` shapes with the file list spelled out per cell (word-split on purpose — no quotes around the list variable).

## Where (parsed into the checklist — every **must change** line must appear as a `-` line in your diff)
* `:30` — (correct) `EXIT=0` — stays; E1 inserts AFTER it
* `:38` — **must change**: `  ".github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml"`
* `:42` — **must change**: `  [ -f "$f" ] || continue`
* `:56` — **must change**: `  echo "OK — no :latest tags found in production-bound configs."`

## Output
Exactly ONE ```diff block with TWO files: `--- a/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-no-latest-tags.sh` / `+++ b/…` (two hunks), then `--- /dev/null` / `+++ b/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/check_no_latest_tags_inputs.test.sh`; paths repo-relative; correct hunk counts; blank context lines keep their leading space.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# CHECK: NO :latest TAGS IN PRODUCTION-BOUND CONFIGS (pen-test H7 partial)
# =============================================================================
# Pen-test H7: dev and demo currently share an ACR (`secuura01demoacr`).
# Separating registries needs work in the demo environment, which is
# off-limits per the project rule "don't touch demo until dev is stable."
#
# As a partial mitigation, we enforce that production-bound configs never
# reference `:latest` — only date-pinned tags. That way, even though dev
# pushes to the same ACR, demo deploys cannot accidentally pull a dev image.
#
# What's checked:
#   - docker-compose.production.yml
#   - deployment/azure/services.bicep / services.parameters.json
#   - deployment/azure/main.bicep / main.parameters.json
#   - .github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml (staging is also pinned in CI)
#
# What's allowed:
#   - docker-compose.yml (dev compose, can use :latest implicit)
#   - docker-compose.local.yml
#   - Dockerfiles (FROM ... :latest is a separate concern; pinned by M16)
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail

ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
cd "$ROOT"

EXIT=0

CHECK_FILES=(
  "docker-compose.production.yml"
  "deployment/azure/services.bicep"
  "deployment/azure/services.parameters.json"
  "deployment/azure/main.bicep"
  "deployment/azure/main.parameters.json"
  ".github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml"
)

for f in "${CHECK_FILES[@]}"; do
  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
  # Match `image: …:latest` or `imageTag: latest` or `:latest"` in JSON.
  # Skip comment-only lines: `#` for yaml/sh, `//` for bicep.
  hits=$(grep -nE '(:latest\b|imageTag[^"]*"latest")' "$f" \
         | grep -vE '^[0-9]+:\s*(#|//)' \
         || true)
  if [ -n "$hits" ]; then
    echo "::error::$f references :latest (pen-test H7 — production must use date-pinned tags):"
    echo "$hits" | sed 's/^/  /'
    EXIT=1
  fi
done

if [ $EXIT -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "OK — no :latest tags found in production-bound configs."
fi

exit $EXIT

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Unit tests for check-script-portability.sh (KS-666).
#
# Every rule is tested BOTH ways: a script that violates it must FAIL, and the legitimate form of
# the same construct must PASS. A rule that only ever passes is indistinguishable from no rule —
# the first draft of the gate itself used `mapfile` (bash 4+, absent here) and then exited 0 with
# an empty file list, reporting clean because it had examined nothing.
#
# No repo scan: each case builds a throwaway directory and points the gate at it via argv.

set -uo pipefail
GATE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)/check-script-portability.sh"
PASS=0; FAIL=0
TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# expect <name> <expected_exit> <script-body> [expected_error_substring]
#
# The 4th argument pins the case to ITS rule. Without it a test passes whenever ANY rule fires,
# so a broken rule hides behind a working one — that mistake let three slot-exclusion mutations
# survive the container-isolation suite earlier today.
expect() {
    local name="$1" want="$2" body="$3" want_err="${4:-}" d out got
    d=$(mktemp -d "$TMP/case.XXXXXX")
    printf '%s\n' "$body" > "$d/candidate.sh"
    out=$("$GATE" "$d" 2>&1); got=$?
    if [[ "$got" != "$want" ]]; then
        FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); echo "  FAIL: $name (expected exit $want, got $got)"; return
    fi
    if [[ -n "$want_err" ]] && ! grep -qF -- "$want_err" <<<"$out"; then
        FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); echo "  FAIL: $name (exit correct, WRONG rule fired — wanted /$want_err/)"; return
    fi
    PASS=$((PASS+1))
}

echo "check_script_portability:"

# --- a clean script passes ----------------------------------------------------
expect "portable script passes" 0 '#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo hello
grep -E "(tests|pass) [0-9]+" out.txt'

# --- rule 1: GNU timeout ------------------------------------------------------
expect "bare \`timeout N\` fails" 1 '#!/usr/bin/env bash
timeout 600 ./thing.sh' "GNU \`timeout\` used"
expect "gtimeout probe passes" 0 '#!/usr/bin/env bash
if command -v gtimeout >/dev/null; then gtimeout 60 ./x; else ./x; fi'
expect "curl --connect-timeout is not a hit" 0 '#!/usr/bin/env bash
curl -s --connect-timeout 3 http://localhost:6882/health'

# --- rule 2: GNU-only flags ---------------------------------------------------
expect "readlink -f fails" 1 '#!/usr/bin/env bash
p=$(readlink -f "$0")' "GNU-only flag"
expect "date -d fails"      1 '#!/usr/bin/env bash
d=$(date -d "yesterday")' "GNU-only flag"

# --- rule 3: stat -----------------------------------------------------------
expect "stat -c alone fails" 1 '#!/usr/bin/env bash
m=$(stat -c %Y "$f")' "no \`stat -f\` fallback"
expect "stat -c with -f fallback passes" 0 '#!/usr/bin/env bash
mtime_of() { stat -c %Y "$1" 2>/dev/null || stat -f %m "$1" 2>/dev/null || echo 0; }'

# --- rule 4: sed -i ---------------------------------------------------------
expect "sed -i without suffix fails" 1 '#!/usr/bin/env bash
sed -i "s/a/b/" file.txt' "backup-suffix"
expect "sed -i '"'""'" passes" 0 '#!/usr/bin/env bash
sed -i "" "s/a/b/" file.txt'

# --- rule 5: glyph-anchored grep ---------------------------------------------
expect "grep \"^. word\" fails" 1 '#!/usr/bin/env bash
npm test 2>&1 | grep -E "^. (tests|pass|fail)"' "anchored on a leading single character"
expect "word-anchored grep passes" 0 '#!/usr/bin/env bash
npm test 2>&1 | grep -aE "(tests|pass|fail) [0-9]+"'

# --- rule 6: background watchdog keeping stdout -------------------------------
expect "unredirected ( sleep ) & fails" 1 '#!/usr/bin/env bash
( sleep 600; kill -TERM $pid ) &' "inherits stdout"
expect "redirected ( sleep ) & passes" 0 '#!/usr/bin/env bash
( sleep 600; kill -TERM $pid ) >/dev/null 2>&1 &'

# --- rule 7: bash 4+ constructs ----------------------------------------------
expect "mapfile fails"     1 '#!/usr/bin/env bash
mapfile -t FILES < <(find . -name "*.sh")' "bash 4+ construct"
expect "readarray fails"   1 '#!/usr/bin/env bash
readarray -t X < list.txt' "bash 4+ construct"
expect "declare -A fails"  1 '#!/usr/bin/env bash
declare -A SERVICES=(
  [api]="services/api/Dockerfile"
)' "bash 4+ construct"
expect "read-loop equivalent passes" 0 '#!/usr/bin/env bash
FILES=()
while IFS= read -r f; do FILES+=("$f"); done < <(find . -name "*.sh")'

# --- comments documenting a hazard are not a hazard ---------------------------
expect "hazard named only in a comment passes" 0 '#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Do not use: timeout 600 ./x   — GNU-only, absent on macOS
# Nor: declare -A map=()        — bash 4+
echo ok'

# --- fixtures must not be scanned (KS-666, found in review by @kksecura) -------
# The gate quotes every hazard it checks for, and so does THIS suite — deliberately, as fixture
# data. Scanning them made 17 of 19 flagged locations self-inflicted, so patching out both real
# defects left the headline count unchanged and the gate could never go green.
d_fix=$(mktemp -d "$TMP/fixtures.XXXXXX")
mkdir -p "$d_fix/__tests__"
printf '%s\n' '#!/usr/bin/env bash' 'echo ok' > "$d_fix/real.sh"
printf '%s\n' '#!/usr/bin/env bash' 'timeout 600 ./x' 'declare -A m=()' 'mapfile -t X < f' \
               'sed -i "s/a/b/" f' 'readlink -f "$0"' > "$d_fix/__tests__/fixtures.test.sh"
out=$("$GATE" "$d_fix" 2>&1); got=$?
if [[ "$got" == "0" ]]; then PASS=$((PASS+1)); else
    FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); echo "  FAIL: hazards inside __tests__/ must not be flagged (got exit $got)"
fi

# ...but the SAME hazards outside __tests__/ still must be.
printf '%s\n' '#!/usr/bin/env bash' 'timeout 600 ./x' > "$d_fix/real.sh"
out=$("$GATE" "$d_fix" 2>&1); got=$?
if [[ "$got" == "1" ]] && grep -qF "GNU \`timeout\` used" <<<"$out"; then PASS=$((PASS+1)); else
    FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); echo "  FAIL: the same hazard outside __tests__/ must still fail (got exit $got)"
fi

# --- non-vacuity --------------------------------------------------------------
# A scan matching no files must NOT report clean: that is the exact way the first draft of this
# gate passed while broken.
d_empty=$(mktemp -d "$TMP/empty.XXXXXX")
out=$("$GATE" "$d_empty" 2>&1); got=$?
if [[ "$got" == "2" ]] && grep -qF "vacuous" <<<"$out"; then PASS=$((PASS+1)); else
    FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); echo "  FAIL: empty corpus must be a usage error, got exit $got"
fi
out=$("$GATE" "$TMP/does-not-exist" 2>&1); got=$?
if [[ "$got" == "2" ]]; then PASS=$((PASS+1)); else
    FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); echo "  FAIL: missing directory must be exit 2, got $got"
fi

echo "check_script_portability: $PASS passed, $FAIL failed"
[[ $FAIL -eq 0 ]]
